missions.title: Rooms and hinges: a small Lean proof built from a fixed prior under three error-signal regimes
missions.label: Rooms and hinges
missions.area: Experiment: machine proof search under controlled error signals
missions.rests_on: a licensed Lean statement, one page of a 1964 paper, Mathlib at one commit, and three logged search runs
missions.record_note: Opened 2026-11-25 with the registration of the first build: Erdős Problem 766, the Dirac–Erdős bound. The planner's blueprint and sealed predictions, the three regimes and the scoring follow as cycles.
record_limits: Nothing has run yet. One theorem, one planner model, one searcher model, one run per regime are planned for the first series.
scope_limits: The experiment measures the Lean bridge from a fixed blueprint to a licensed statement; it does not measure mathematical discovery, and it does not check the mathematics of the 1964 argument.
No human-only Lean proof of this statement exists to serve as a control; the existing proof is machine-assisted.

opening.spoken: This record holds an experiment: a small proof is built from a fixed prior, a planner predicts the cost of every step before any search, and the same plan is searched three times with the error signal set differently each time.

short_version.spoken: The shape of a recent machine-built proof of the Riemann hypothesis suggested a search sized to a fast exact error signal, with retries concentrated at the joins. That reading came from one archive with no attempt log. Here the prior is fixed, the plan is drawn once by one model, the cost of each step is predicted and sealed, and a second model searches the plan under full Lean feedback, under accept or reject only, and with no checker until the end. The first target is the Dirac–Erdős bound, Erdős Problem 766, whose Lean statement and only Lean proof both appeared after the searcher model's training cutoff.

what_happened.spoken: On 25 November 2026 the target was chosen from the untracked-claims backlog, the pinned Lean project was built in a virtual machine, the check tool was dry-run, and the registration with its predictions was committed. No planner or searcher has run.

new.spoken: a registered experiment with eight predictions on the record, and a sealed-prediction protocol for the planner

certainty_statement.spoken: Nothing is accepted or certified. The registration is on the record and the runs are owed.

cycles.hypothesis: With the plan fixed, the search's cost and shape are set by the error signal at the joins: full Lean feedback gives small checked steps and search residue, accept-or-reject costs more attempts for the same result, and no checker until the end produces a fit (a changed statement, an added hypothesis, a sorry or a weaker variant) rather than a proof of the statement as given; and a planner's sealed per-step cost predictions miss most at the joins.

preregistered.question: Given a fixed prior and a licensed Lean statement, how far does a planner's per-step cost prediction miss the search's actual cost, and how do step size, retries and fit indicators change across three error-signal regimes?
preregistered.rule: predictions P1–P8 as written in the registration; a miss is recorded as a miss; the planner's per-node predictions are sealed by hash before the first searcher runs and opened after the last
predictions: P1 R1 and R2 pass the comparator; R3 does not pass as first declared final
P2 median attempts per node in R2 ≥ 1.5 × R1
P3 the planner's median log2 error is larger at joins than at leaves in R1
P4 R3 shows at least one fit indicator; R1 none surviving the comparator
P5 R1 and R2 each leave at least one unused declaration; R3 none
P7 R1 uses fewer total tokens than R2
P8 R1 depth within 2 of the control's

cycles.spoken: Nervous Machine registered the first build of the rooms experiment: the Dirac–Erdős bound from one page of Erdős and Mathlib at one commit, a planner on Claude Opus 5.5 with sealed per-step predictions, and a searcher on Claude Fable 5.1 under three error-signal regimes. The instruments are committed and hashed; the runs can begin.
